title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is not part of the de Rham / divided-power notes around it. It is a page of a typescript, numbered '- 42 - IX', of SGA 7 I, Exposé IX (Grothendieck, 'Modèles de Néron et monodromie'), §4.3. That section proves that traces of Galois elements on Tate modules of abelian varieties with semi-stable reduction are rational integers independent of ℓ. The sheet was presumably reused as scrap paper, or misfiled, among the 1975–76 manuscript notes.

Setting. A_K is an abelian variety over a henselian discretely valued field K with semi-stable reduction. The identity component of the special fibre of the Néron model is an extension A*_o of an abelian variety B*_o by a torus T*_o. M' is the character group of the relevant (dual) torus, isomorphic to Z^μ.

Filtration. By (4.2.10), V_ℓ(A_K) = U_ℓ carries the monodromy filtration. Its graded pieces are T_ℓ(T), T_ℓ(B) and the dual piece Hom(T_ℓ(T'), Z_ℓ(1)). Hence the trace of g ∈ Γ splits into three terms.

a) g in inertia. Inertia acts on the reductions through k'-automorphisms and trivially on Z_ℓ(1). This gives (4.3.0): Tr g_U = Tr g_B + Tr g_T + Tr g^{-1}_T. One must show that the two geometric traces are integers independent of ℓ.
- Abelian part: Weil's theorem that the characteristic polynomial of an endomorphism on T_ℓ has integer coefficients independent of ℓ.
- Torus part: trivial, because T_ℓ(T) ≅ M̌'⊗Z_ℓ(1). The trace is that of the contragredient of an integral representation on M' ≅ Z^μ.

b) g mapping to f_q^n in π_o (geometric Frobenius power). The Tate twist contributes the factor q^n, giving (4.3.1): Tr g_U = Tr g_B + Tr g_T + q^n Tr g^{-1}_T.

Both cases reduce to Lemma 4.3.2. Let k = F̄_p, A a commutative group scheme of finite type over k, and g a semilinear automorphism of A, compatible with a q-power Frobenius on Spec k. Then the trace on T_ℓ(A) is an integer independent of ℓ. The proof goes via dévissage into abelian, toric and unipotent/finite parts, using the fact that a semilinear map over a finite field descends after taking powers / Lang. The Kleiman reference [14, 2.8] is to 'Algebraic cycles and the Weil conjectures' (Dix exposés), cited for a proof of a preceding statement.
errors: The third trace term in (4.3.0)/(4.3.1) should concern the dual torus piece (the character group M' / dual torus T'). The image shows T*_o in all places, which may be a notational simplification or a typo in the draft.

The phrase 'la trace cherchée est contragrédiente de celle de cette dernière représentation' is loose. It means that the representation is the contragredient (twisted by Z_ℓ(1)), so the trace is that of g^{-1} on M'.

ideas.what: Trace of Galois/inertia elements on V_ℓ of an abelian variety with semistable reduction decomposes along the monodromy filtration into abelian, toric and dual-toric terms; it is an integer independent of ℓ
ideas.modern_name: Independence of ℓ for semistable abelian varieties (SGA 7 IX §4.3)

ideas.what: Integrality and ℓ-independence of the characteristic polynomial of endomorphisms of abelian varieties
ideas.modern_name: Weil's theorem on the characteristic polynomial of endomorphisms

ideas.what: Tate module of a torus as dual character lattice twisted by Z_ℓ(1)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typescript page of the published SGA 7 Exposé IX §4.3, interleaved (likely reused as scrap paper) with the unrelated divided-power de Rham notes. Its content is fully published and credited to Grothendieck.
transcription_corrections: The first trace in (4.3.0) is written Tr g_{U_ℓ} in the typescript, while (4.3.1) has g_{U,ℓ}. This is an inconsistency in the original, not in the transcription.
The 'A ↦ A*_o^o ⊗_{k'} k̄' in the reduction step denotes the identity component (A*_o)^o base-changed to k̄.
The page is a typed page of SGA 7 Exp. IX (page 42), not a manuscript page of the PD de Rham notes. The archive stamp reads 360, with folio 172 in pencil.
